svg.title: Continuous Delivery
svg.desc: Continuous Delivery. Keep every change releasable: a deployment pipeline builds once, tests in stages and promotes the same artifact to production. Step 1, A release everyone fears: Every 4 weeks: 140 commits at once, a build per environment and 40 manual steps on Saturday night. Step 2, The deployment pipeline: Commit 7f3c2a: the image is built once in 6 min, then the same digest is promoted stage by stage. Step 3, Stop the line, ship small: A red acceptance test stops the line: 1.43.0 is never promoted, and a revert goes in within minutes. Step 4, Pitfalls and limits: A 75-min run, flaky tests and hand-patched staging erode trust; schemas need expand and contract.

g.text: Every 4 weeks: 140 commits at once, a build per environment and 40 manual steps on Saturday night.
Commit 7f3c2a: the image is built once in 6 min, then the same digest is promoted stage by stage.
A red acceptance test stops the line: 1.43.0 is never promoted, and a revert goes in within minutes.
A 75-min run, flaky tests and hand-patched staging erode trust; schemas need expand and contract.
deployment pipeline: every commit to main runs it; the only route to production
continuous delivery: a person clicks Deploy · continuous deployment: every green build ships
still the only route to production, approvals included
no shared artifact: every environment gets a fresh build of the branch
Sat 22:00 → Sun 04:30 · a 40-step runbook · 6 people on a call
Painful, so it happens rarely, so every release gets bigger.
Any green build can go to production with one click.
red at 20 min: the line stops
main @ c19e57, a revert of 8d41e0 pushed 4 min after the red → checkout:1.43.1
Small changes, so a red is quick to find. Fixing it comes before any new work.
main: 9 commits in one run. If it goes red, which one broke it?
Over an hour per run: people batch their changes again.
